extracted.intended_audience: recipients of Federal transit financial assistance, private charter operators (registered charter providers), qualified human service organizations, and FTA officials/ombudsman
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements and procedures under 49 CFR part 604 governing when and how recipients may provide charter service, including definitions, exceptions, registration and notification rules, recordkeeping, petitions, advisory opinions, cease-and-desist orders, and complaint procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and scope of part 604
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of this part is to implement 49 U.S.C. 5323(d), which protects private charter operators from unauthorized competition from recipients of Federal financial assistance under the Federal Transit Laws. This subpart specifies which entities shall comply with the regulations in this part; defines terms used in this part; explains procedures for an exemption from this part; and sets out the contents of a charter service agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains overall intent: protect private charter operators and set compliance scope. Use to determine whether an entity or activity falls under part 604.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability and enumerated exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: The requirements apply to recipients of Federal financial assistance under the Federal Transit Laws, except specific categories enumerated in paragraphs (b) through (g) such as transporting certain officials, non-FTA funded activities of private charter operators, emergency responses, and program-purpose uses under certain statutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Lists specific non-applicability situations (e.g., employee transport, non-FTA-funded private operator activity, emergency actions, program-purposes under 49 U.S.C. 5310/5311). Use these to determine if a recipient is exempt from part 604 for a given trip or activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'Charter service'
rubrics_metrics.description: Charter service means, but does not include demand response service to individuals: (1) Transportation provided by a recipient at the request of a third party for the exclusive use of a bus or van for a negotiated price, with characteristic features listed (third party pays, fares collected by third party, not part of regular service, third party determines origin/destination/scheduling); or (2) Transportation provided by a recipient to the public for events or functions that occur on an irregular basis or for a limited duration and either (i) a premium fare is charged greater than usual fixed route fare; or (ii) the service is paid for in whole or in part by a third party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the test for distinguishing charter service from demand-response or regular public transit; if service meets either (1) or (2) conditions, it is charter service for regulatory purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charter service hours definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Charter service hours means total hours operated by buses or vans while in charter service including: (1) Hours operated while carrying passengers for hire; plus (2) Associated deadhead hours.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this definition when calculating annual limits (e.g., Government Officials exception) and reporting charter activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charter Service Agreement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient seeking Federal assistance to acquire or operate public transportation equipment or facilities shall enter into a 'Charter Service Agreement' which incorporates 49 CFR part 604 by reference and commits the recipient and sub-recipients/contractors using FTA-funded vehicles to comply with part 604.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agreement is contained in FTA Certifications and Assurances and becomes part of the Grant or Cooperative Agreement once funds are received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government officials exception conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may provide charter service to government officials for official business if it: (1) provides service in its geographic service area; (2) does not generate revenue from the charter service except as required by law; and (3) records specific trip details (organization name, date/time, number of passengers including number of officials, origin/destination/trip length, fee collected if any, vehicle number).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Additional limits: annual limit of 80 charter service hours; recipient may petition Administrator for more hours with specified supporting information; requests posted to Government Officials Exception docket for public review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualified Human Service Organization (QHSO) eligibility and registration
rubrics_metrics.description: QHSOs that seek free or reduced rate services and do not receive funds from human services Federal programs listed in CCAM Program Inventory must register on FTA's charter registration website by providing specified information (name, contact, geographic service area, financial info and tax-exempt status, state/local funding, narrative describing trip types and mission consistency). A QHSO is eligible if it receives funds from CCAM-listed programs or registers at least 60 days before requested service and verifies receipt on the website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registered QHSOs must keep information current (update at least every two years). Registered charter providers may challenge QHSO eligibility via complaint procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registration requirements for private charter operators
rubrics_metrics.description: To be a registered charter provider, private operators must register on FTA's charter registration website providing: company name/address/phone/email/fax; Federal and, if available, State motor carrier identifying number; geographic service areas by zip code; number of buses/vans owned; certification of valid insurance; and whether willing to provide free/reduced services to registered QHSOs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to provide required information may lead FTA to refuse posting. Registered providers have standing to file complaints and must update information no less frequently than every two years.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient notification to registered charter providers (timing and content)
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon receiving a charter request, if the recipient seeks to rely on §604.9, it shall provide email notice to registered charter providers in its geographic area: send by close of business same day (or next business day if request received after 2 p.m.); include customer contact, requested date, approximate passengers, equipment type (bus/van), trip itinerary and approximate duration; if service meets paragraph (2) of the charter definition, include the intended fare.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipient must retain electronic copy of the email and list of providers sent notice for at least three years. If email undeliverable, send facsimile and keep records of undeliverable notice and fax confirmation.

rubrics_metrics.name: When no registered charter provider responds
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may provide charter service if no registered provider responds to notice within: (1) 72 hours for service requested in less than 30 days; or (2) 14 calendar days for service requested 30 days or more.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipient may not provide service if a registered provider has indicated interest and informed recipient. After providing service under this provision, recipient must record group contact info, date/time, number of passengers, origin/destination/trip length, fee collected if any, and vehicle number.

rubrics_metrics.name: Leasing FTA-funded equipment and drivers to registered charter providers
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may lease its FTA-funded equipment and drivers to registered charter providers only if: (1) the private charter operator is registered; (2) the registered provider owns and operates buses/vans in a charter business; (3) the registered provider received a request exceeding its available capacity (vehicles or accessible vehicles); and (4) the registered provider has exhausted all available vehicles of all registered providers in the recipient's geographic service area.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipient leasing vehicles/drivers shall record the registered provider's contact, number/types/IDs of vehicles leased, and documentation presented by the registered provider supporting the four conditions. If a leasing provider has filed a complaint to remove another provider, it need not exhaust vehicles from that other provider while complaint pending.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agreements with registered charter providers
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may provide charter service directly consistent with an agreement entered into with all registered charter providers in its geographic area. If a new provider registers after the agreement, the recipient may continue under previous agreement up to 90 days without agreement with the new provider. Any party to an agreement may cancel with 90 days notice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agreements must involve all registered providers to rely on this exception; watch 90-day transition and cancellation rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petitions to the Administrator for exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient may petition the Administrator for an exception to provide charter service directly for events of regional/national significance, hardship (limited to small/non-urbanized areas), or unique and time-sensitive events in the public interest. The petition must include event details, type of service/equipment, anticipated charter hours and vehicles/duration; for regional/national events include consultation description with registered providers and certification of exhaustion of registered providers and must be submitted at least 90 days before event; hardship petitions require showing that a registered provider's deadhead time exceeds total trip time and description of hardship; unique/time-sensitive petitions must explain uniqueness/time-sensitivity and public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrator will review, may seek additional info, and issue written decision posted to Petitions docket. Exceptions are effective only for the described event. Send petition via specified email and retain approval copy at least three years and include in quarterly website report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting and recordkeeping for exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients providing service under exceptions must maintain required notice and records electronically for at least three years and include a clear statement identifying which exception was relied upon. Records must be posted on the FTA charter registration website 30 days after each calendar quarter (Jan 30, Apr 30, Jul 30, Oct 30). A single document/charter log may include all trips for the quarter. Specific origin/destination info may be excluded for safety/security if reason described and generalized info provided instead.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Records may be maintained in other formats in addition to electronic. Retention and timely posting are mandatory; include justification if excluding sensitive trip details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recipient duties regarding charter registration website competency
rubrics_metrics.description: Each recipient shall ensure that its affected employees and contractors have the necessary competency to effectively use the FTA charter registration website.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Imposes an obligation on recipients to train or otherwise ensure personnel can perform registration, notification, reporting, and recordkeeping tasks on the website.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advisory opinion request form and content
rubrics_metrics.description: An interested party may request an advisory opinion on specific factual events. A request must be in specified form to Chief Counsel and include: full statement of all facts and legal points relevant; an affirmation that the request includes all data, favorable or unfavorable; and a certification of service on interested parties with names/addresses and method of service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chief Counsel may request additional information. Requests may be denied for incomplete information, matters not suitable for advisory opinion, matters covered by prior advisory opinion/regulation, or if not in public interest. Requests should be filed electronically to the specified docket or emailed to the Chief Counsel address.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing and timeliness of advisory opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chief Counsel shall make every effort to respond within ten days of receipt of a request that complies with the form requirements. The decision shall be sent to the interested party, the docket, and the recipient if appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisory opinions must be filed in the Advisory Opinion/Cease and Desist docket or sent to FTA's dockets office; Chief Counsel may seek additional info during processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect and limits of advisory opinions
rubrics_metrics.description: An advisory opinion represents the formal position of FTA on a matter and obligates the agency to follow it until amended or revoked (except as provided in §604.25). It may be used in administrative or court proceedings to illustrate acceptable/unacceptable procedures or standards but is not a legal requirement and is limited to the factual circumstances. Advisory opinions issued under this section are not binding on a Presiding Official conducting a proceeding under subpart I. Oral or informal written advice does not constitute an advisory opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advisory opinions can guide parties but do not create enforceable rights beyond their factual scope; informal staff statements are not advisory opinions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requesting a cease and desist order (contents and denial grounds)
rubrics_metrics.description: An interested party may request a cease and desist order as part of an advisory opinion request. The request must describe need for the order, a detailed description of the likely lost business opportunity and how public interest is served by avoiding/ameliorating it (registered providers must distinguish their loss from others), and a detailed description of efforts to notify the recipient of potential violation (names, contact info, dates/times, responses). Requests may be denied for incomplete information, matters not suitable, matters covered by prior cease and desist order, or if not in public interest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A recipient subject to such a request has three business days to respond with a point-by-point rebuttal. Timing begins when the request is filed in the docket or with the Chief Counsel's Office, whichever is sooner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chief Counsel decision standard for cease and desist orders
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chief Counsel may grant a cease and desist order if the interested party demonstrates, by a preponderance of the evidence, that the planned provision of charter service by a recipient would violate this part. In making the decision, the Chief Counsel shall consider the signed, sworn request's facts, applicable statutes, regulations, agreements, and any other relevant information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets evidentiary standard (preponderance of the evidence) and enumerates factors to consider in deciding whether to issue an order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of issuance of a cease and desist order
rubrics_metrics.description: Issuance of a cease and desist order against a recipient is considered an aggravating factor in determining remedies for future findings of noncompliance with this part if the recipient provides the service described in the cease and desist order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients should treat issuance as a serious enforcement marker that may increase sanctions for subsequent violations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complaint requirements for removal of registrations
rubrics_metrics.description: A recipient, registered charter provider, or authorized representative may challenge a listing by filing a complaint that: states the name/address of each subject entity; provides a concise but complete statement of facts supporting removal; files electronically to the specified Charter Service Removal Complaints docket; serves by email/fax (or overnight mail with receipt confirmation) and attaches supporting documents; files within 90 days of discovering facts meriting removal; and contains the specified certification of service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: FTA expects informal resolution attempts before formal complaints. Complaints must meet procedural requirements (docket filing, service, attachments, timeliness) to be considered.
